question.text: In an experiment to determine the acceleration due to gravity g, the formula used for the time period of a periodic motion is <math><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>g</mi></mrow></mfrac></msqrt><mo>.</mo></math> The values of R and r are measured to be <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>60</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi><mi>m</mi><mi> </mi><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi> </mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi>m</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi></math> respectively. In five successive measurements, the time period is found to be 0.52s, 0.56s, 0.57s, 0.54s and 0.59s. The least count of the watch used for the measurement of time period is 0.01s. Which of the following statements (s) is (are) true?

options.text: The error in the measurement of r is 10%.
The error in the measurement of T is 3.57 %.
The error in the measurement of T is 2%.
The error in the determined value of g is 11%.
